purpose: Curated history of things that broke and decisions that were made, so neither gets re-investigated or re-litigated from scratch. Ingested into homelab.db and queryable via the hl_incidents MCP tool ('symptom X — have we seen this?'). Hand-edited; every entry cites where the full detail lives.

conventions.kind: incident (something broke) | decision (a choice that should not be silently reversed)
conventions.date: ISO date the event happened or the decision was taken
conventions.source: where the authoritative detail lives — a runbook, rule, or code path

incidents.title: noblenumbat unreachable — cooling, not software
incidents.symptom: Whole host unreachable. Jellyfin and the *arr stack all down at once, which reads like a container or compose fault.
incidents.cause: A cooling problem took the machine down. Nothing in the media stack was at fault.
incidents.resolution: Physical intervention. Suspect hardware/thermal before debugging containers when EVERY service on one host goes at once.

incidents.title: noblenumbat never came back from a cockpit reboot
incidents.symptom: A reboot issued from the webapp cockpit succeeded in sending, but the host did not return to the network.
incidents.cause: Not diagnosed remotely — the host was unreachable by every path.
incidents.resolution: Needed a physical power cycle. A remote reboot on this host is not safely reversible without hands on the box.

incidents.title: Skills and rules destroyed by rm -rf on a clean-looking working copy
incidents.symptom: homelab/agentic/ content vanished when a ptm4 working copy was deleted after `git status` showed clean.
incidents.cause: `git status` hides ignored AND untracked content. At the time homelab/agentic/ was gitignored, so a clean status meant nothing about what was on disk.
incidents.resolution: Recovered partly from transcripts and git. homelab/agentic/ is now TRACKED (verified 2026-07-25), and the PreToolUse guard hard-denies rm -rf of a repo working copy. Always run `git status --ignored --porcelain` and `git clean -ndx` before deleting any working copy.

incidents.title: "All the servers are down" — two DHCP servers racing
incidents.symptom: Widespread apparent outage: clients cannot resolve names or reach services, but the servers themselves are healthy.
incidents.cause: The router's DHCP server was enabled alongside Pi-hole's. Clients that won the race got the router's lease and therefore the wrong DNS.
incidents.resolution: Pi-hole is the only DHCP and DNS server for the LAN. Router DHCP must stay OFF. Symptom-to-cause is non-obvious: healthy hosts plus universal client failure means DHCP/DNS, not the services.

incidents.title: Gluetun NAT-PMP forwarded port dies silently
incidents.symptom: Torrents stop connecting. Gluetun itself looks healthy and the VPN is up.
incidents.cause: The NAT-PMP port forward expires or is lost without Gluetun reporting an error, and qBittorrent's listen port no longer matches it.
incidents.resolution: vpn-stack-heal watchdog (every 2 min since 2026-07-11) re-establishes the forward and updates qBittorrent. Check /var/lib/vpn-stack-heal/status.json before assuming a torrent fault. Five containers share gluetun's netns, so stopping it takes them all down by design.

incidents.title: "4 services down" panel while every container was healthy
incidents.symptom: The dashboard reported several services down; checking the containers showed all of them running fine.
incidents.cause: opti's systemd-resolved had fallen back to 1.1.1.1, which cannot resolve the .lan names the checks use. The checks failed on name resolution, not on the services.
incidents.resolution: A ~lan drop-in pins Pi-hole as the resolver for .lan on opti. When a health panel disagrees with `docker ps`, suspect resolution from the checking host.

incidents.title: Stale CIFS handles after a ZFS dataset change on opti
incidents.symptom: Containers on noblenumbat keep working, then fail the moment they are recreated — with paths that plainly exist on opti.
incidents.cause: Changing an opti ZFS dataset invalidates noblenumbat's CIFS subpath handles. Running processes coast on their open handles; anything that reopens the path fails.
incidents.resolution: umount and let autofs re-trigger the mount. The nn-deploy workflow has a preflight check for this now.

incidents.title: network-report flagged android with no default gateway (false positive)
incidents.symptom: Critical finding: gateway null and unreachable — while the same report row showed internet:true and successful DNS lookups.
incidents.cause: Android routes per-app/per-uid through tables an unprivileged Termux process cannot see, so `ip route show default` legitimately returns nothing there.
incidents.resolution: default_gateway() falls back to `ip route get 1.1.1.1`, which asks the kernel what it would actually use. A finding that contradicts other fields in the same report is a collector bug until proven otherwise.

incidents.title: Deploy deadlock when the API smoke ran before the bots were rebuilt
incidents.symptom: A bot response-shape change could never deploy: the smoke test failed against the old bot, so the rebuild that would fix it never ran.
incidents.cause: Ordering. rpi-deploy.yml smoked the API before rebuilding the bot containers.
incidents.resolution: rpi-deploy.yml must rebuild bots BEFORE the API smoke. Any gate that runs before the step that satisfies it is a deadlock, not a check.

incidents.title: Local collector fixes silently reverted
incidents.symptom: A fix made to a collector on opti stops being in effect some time later, with no one having changed it back.
incidents.cause: Collectors run from BOTH a GitHub Actions checkout (the */30 workflow) and opti's working copy. The checkout overwrites what the working copy has until the change is pushed.
incidents.resolution: Push collector changes; do not rely on a local edit persisting.

decisions.title: The gateway is a TP-Link Archer, not a Verizon router
decisions.symptom: Earlier docs described a "Verizon router"; that hardware does not exist here.
decisions.resolution: Confirmed 2026-07-31: the gateway at 192.168.1.1 is a TP-Link Archer, and it is also the WireGuard server. Correct any doc that still says otherwise.

decisions.title: noblenumbat is not a code server — reverted
decisions.symptom: A second ptm4 clone existed on noblenumbat as a coding target.
decisions.cause: Trialled, then reverted: two working copies of the same repo invite exactly the clobber class above.
decisions.resolution: The primary (and only) working copy is the opti CIFS mount at /home/ptm/opti/ptm/repo/ptm4. The noblenumbat clone no longer exists — do not send edits there.

decisions.title: Jellyfin API token rotation declined
decisions.symptom: The Jellyfin token used by the discord-jellyfin bot was proposed for rotation.
decisions.resolution: Peter declined. Do not rotate it as a drive-by 'improvement'; raise it as its own decision if the risk changes.

decisions.title: hltv.org is the only CS2 source; VRS is the only ranking
decisions.cause: n/a — a deliberate choice about data provenance.
decisions.resolution: The HLTV bot uses hltv.org exclusively, and Valve Regional Standings (/valve-ranking/teams) as the ONLY ranking — never HLTV's own ranking. A full Chromium is required to pass Cloudflare; headless-shell never does.

decisions.title: The S10's bootloader is permanently locked — no reimage, no root
decisions.symptom: Options that assume root or a custom image are not available on this device.
decisions.cause: SM-G973U with a permanently locked bootloader.
decisions.resolution: Work within Termux, unrooted. Privileged commands go through adb over LOOPBACK ONLY, never from another host. Hardening applied 2026-08-19: phantom process killer off, DHCP reservation, keepalive crons.

decisions.title: homelab.db lives outside the Samba-exported tree
decisions.cause: SQLite WAL requires same-host shared memory; over CIFS it is unsupported by design, including read-only opens.
decisions.resolution: The database is on ZFS dataset red/opsdb, deliberately NOT under red/fs, so it is unreachable over the share. tux and rpi query :9100 instead. Backups take the VACUUM INTO snapshot, never the live db + -wal pair.
